authoredNote: PERL-ONTOLOGY. Four composition shapes and two `has` shapes in fifteen lines, because each was a place where the lane read a SLOT NAME as a DECLARATION and the numbers were too small for any count to notice. Line numbers are read off the numbered source above.
rationale: A role composition is a NAME LIST, and Moose/Moo write it in four shapes that look alike and are not. (1) `with 'R'` — one name. (2) `with qw(A B)` — ONE `quoted_word_list` node, so reading only its first word published A and dropped B: measured on moo, 6 of 94 `implements` rows and 5 of 109 `extends` rows on 142 files. (3) `with 'A', { -excludes => [...], -alias => {...} }, 'B'` — the MIXED form, where a bare `{ ... }` among the names is a MODIFIER specification and the modifier names live one level deeper inside it. Reading every word published them as roles: measured on Moose-2.4000/t/roles/role_conflict_detection.t:139 (`implements My::Test8 -> -alias`) and t/roles/more_alias_and_exclude.t:47. (4) `with 'A' => {...}, 'B' => {...}` — the fat-comma SPECIFICATION form, where the roles are the top-level KEYS. All three of 2-4 are PERL-MR4's rule — a fat-comma key is a SLOT name, not a declaration — stated for role composition, and all three were wrong on the analyzer AND on the independent oracle at the same time. The two `has` rows are the same class on the attribute side: a `has` specification's fat-comma keys are OPTION names (`clearer`, `predicate` on line 11), and the attribute name itself is ONE literal read verbatim (`has spaces` on line 12, which the word splitter truncated to `has`).

expectRelationships.note: tier: the source states this edge: a declaration or a written name, confidence >= 0.9
the FIRST word of a `qw(...)` node. Only this one existed before the fix: the node is ONE `quoted_word_list` and `[0]` took one name from it.
the SECOND word of the SAME node, on the same line. Reading only the first loses every role after the first in every `qw()` composition in a corpus.
the MIXED form: a bare `{ ... }` among the names is a MODIFIER specification. The modifier names are one level deeper and are not roles.
the fat-comma SPECIFICATION form: the roles are the top-level KEYS, so they are read with `fatCommaKeys` and never by descending into a value.
a `has` attribute name is ONE literal, read verbatim from the grammar's own `content`

a name containing a SPACE. The word splitter exists for `qw(a b)`, which IS a list; a quoted attribute name is one name whatever it contains, and the pre-fix behaviour truncated this to `has` — worse than publishing nothing, because `has` is a real perl function.

forbidRelationships.note: line 9: a MODIFIER name, not a role
line 9 and 10: the same modifier with the sigil stripped
line 9/10: the alias TARGET inside the modifier hash is the name the modifier creates, not a role
line 9: a role the -excludes modifier removes. It is named, and it is not composed.
line 11: a `has` OPTION name. The pre-fix shape published it as a property — measured on Moose-2.4000/t/accessor-pred-clear.t:13.
line 12: the TRUNCATED form of `has spaces`, which is worse than nothing because `has` is a real perl function and a `bb_impact` on it would reach every Moose class
